item.title: Endpoint maximal estimates for the half-wave propagator
item.dc:creator: Bowen An, Wenjuan Li, Huiju Wang

item.title: Diagonal and branchwise criteria for universal Fourier series
item.description: arXiv:2610.27348v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize diagonal profiles admitting universal real trigonometric Fourier series with factors in $\mathcal E_s=\bigcap_{p>s}\ell^p$ and $\ell^{s,q}$, $2\le s<\infty$, $1\le q\le\infty$. For nonincreasing profiles we obtain exact dyadic criteria and logarithmic endpoints. For independently regular odd/even sine/cosine branches we characterize simultaneous subseries, sign, and rearrangement universality for finite almost-everywhere targets. One function in every $L^p$, $1\le p<2$, supplies the coefficients. A separation example admits this realization although every compatible nonincreasing majorant with bounded relative cost belongs to $\ell^1$. Residue-class decompositions extend the criterion; a weakest-model condition permits extended-real rearrangement targets. A Walsh--Paley analogue gives the same diagonal tests for ternary modifications. Trigonometric realization uses Pogosyan's majorant theorem; the multiplier, factorization, projection-transfer, separation, and Walsh Fourier-origin arguments are proved here.
item.dc:creator: Sergo A. Episkoposian

item.title: Sharp estimates for imaginary powers of discrete Laplacians
item.description: arXiv:2610.27385v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\Delta_{\rm d}$ be the nonnegative discrete Laplacian on $\mathbb Z^d$. We prove that, for $0<p\le1$, \[ \|\Delta_{\rm d}^{i\gamma}\|_{H^p_{\Delta_{\rm d}}\to H^p_{\Delta_{\rm d}}} \simeq (1+|\gamma|)^{d(1/p-1/2)}, \] and, for $1<p<\infty$, \[ \|\Delta_{\rm d}^{i\gamma}\|_{\ell^p\to\ell^p} \simeq (1+|\gamma|)^{d|1/p-1/2|}. \] The estimates are sharp with respect to the exponent of $1+|\gamma|$. We also explain why the general spectral multiplier theorem and the usual Calder\'on--Zygmund approach do not give the sharp power.
item.dc:creator: The Anh Bui, The Quan Bui, Thanh Tinh Cao

item.title: A self-dual Dunkl wavelet frame and Besov--Triebel--Lizorkin spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.27391v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a self-dual Parseval wavelet frame associated with the Dunkl transform and use it to characterize the corresponding Besov and Triebel-Lizorkin spaces for arbitrary smoothness and the full range of admissible indices. We also establish differential atomic decompositions with atoms supported on dilated Euclidean dyadic cubes, satisfying ordinary derivative estimates and polynomial moment indices. A key difficulty is the interaction between Euclidean dyadic cubes and the orbit geometry associated with the Dunkl operators. As applications, we obtain fractional chain rules and a Jackson inequality for nonlinear wavelet approximation in $L^p(dw)$.
item.dc:creator: The Anh Bui

item.title: Quicksilver Asymptotics and Pole Arrays for $q$-Painlev\'e II
item.description: arXiv:2610.27525v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct local families of solutions of the $q$-difference second Painlev\'e equation that vanish at infinity with a common algebraic expansion, parameterised by the amplitude of an exponentially small correction. Considering an appropriate boundary region, a formal expansion that retains two independently excited exponential perturbations is developed, and subsequent transseries summation predicts the location of simple poles. Adopting a $q$-theta function realisation of the exponential factors, we prove an asymptotic pole-location formula for a one-parameter family of true solutions. These poles approach the aforementioned boundaries where exponential behaviour fundamentally changes, providing an analogue of pole arrays near anti-Stokes directions in classical Painlev\'e asymptotics.
item.dc:creator: Joshua Holroyd

item.title: Global Mizohata-Takeuchi for Indicator Weights of Bounded Complexity in $\mathbb{R}^2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.27659v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the global Mizohata-Takeuchi estimate for bounded complexity weights in $\mathbb{R}^2$ and an arbitrary $C^2$ uniformly convex curve on the Fourier side, with an implied constant depending only on the complexity and the curve. A version with a logarithmic loss follows from a short argument using the $T^*T$ method and the main estimate of Basu, Guo, Zhang, and Zorin-Kranich (2026). The main effort of this paper is devoted to removing the logarithmic factor. To achieve this, we use tools from semialgebraic geometry and adapt and develop ideas of Ricci and Stein (1987). As a by-product, we obtain a uniform geometric inequality for planar regions of bounded complexity that may be of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Jiaqi Hao, Ruyi Wang, Ruixiang Zhang

item.title: Sharp boundedness criteria for nonnegative kernels on regular curves in the Heisenberg group
item.description: arXiv:2610.27730v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we study singular integrals associated with the nonnegative kernels \[ K_\alpha(x,y,z)=\frac{|z|^{\alpha/2}}{\|(x,y,z)\|^{\alpha+1}}, \qquad \alpha>0, \] in the first Heisenberg group $\mathbb H$, where $\|\cdot\|$ denotes the Kor\'anyi norm. This family was introduced by Chousionis and Li. We first show that there exists a compact $1$-Ahlfors regular horizontal $C^1$ curve $E\subset\mathbb H$ such that the singular integrals associated with $K_\alpha$ are unbounded on $L^2(E)$ for every $0<\alpha<4$. This extends the counterexamples of Chousionis, Li and Zhang from $0<\alpha<2$ to the full range $0<\alpha<4$. Combined with the boundedness theorem of F\"assler and Orponen for $\alpha\ge4$, our result determines the exact range of exponents for boundedness on every $1$-Ahlfors regular curve. We also consider the more general kernels \[ K_\Phi(p)=\frac{1}{\|p\|} \Phi\!\left(\frac{|z|^{1/2}}{\|p\|}\right), \qquad p=(x,y,z)\neq0, \] where $\Phi:[0,1]\to[0,\infty)$ is continuous and nondecreasing, with $\Phi(0)=0$. We show that the associated singular integral is $L^2$-bounded on every $1$-Ahlfors regular curve if and only if $\Phi(u)=O(u^4)$ as $u\to0$. When this condition fails, we construct a compact $1$-Ahlfors regular horizontal $C^1$ curve on which the operator is unbounded. The curves in both constructions can be chosen as horizontal lifts of planar $C^1$ graphs with arbitrarily small slope.
item.dc:creator: Lingxiao Zhang

item.title: The strong type endpoint estimate for the local spherical maximal function
item.description: arXiv:2610.27803v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $p_d=(d^2+1)/(d(d-1))$ and $q_d=(d^2+1)/(d-1)$. We prove that the local spherical maximal operator $\sup_{1\leq t\leq 2}|f*d\sigma_t|$ is bounded from $L^{p_d}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ to $L^{q_d}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for every $d\geq 2$. Previously only the restricted weak type estimate was known at this endpoint. Together with known results, this completes the characterization of the strong type $L^p\to L^q$ bounds for the local spherical maximal operator. We also prove the maximal estimate \[ \Big\|\sup_{t\in\mathbb{R}}|e^{it\sqrt{-\Delta}}f|\Big\|_{L^{2(d+1)/(d-1)}(\mathbb{R}^d)} \lesssim\|f\|_{\dot H^{d/(d+1)}(\mathbb{R}^d)} \] for the wave equation at the critical exponent. Both results are obtained by exploiting the gain in bilinear estimates that comes from the interaction between high and low frequencies.
item.dc:creator: Sanghyuk Lee, Shuijiang Zhao

item.title: Almgren minimality of products of simplex-skeleton cones
item.description: arXiv:2610.27845v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove that for every $m,n\geq 2$, the orthogonal product $S_m\times S_n\subset\R^m\times\R^n$ is an Almgren minimal cone of dimension $m+n-2$, where $S_k\subset\R^k$ is the cone over the $(k-2)$-skeleton of a regular $k$-simplex. Lawlor and Morgan \cite{LM94} proved the minimality of each $S_k$ by paired calibrations, while Guy David \cite{DJT, GD13} later raised the general question whether products of Almgren minimal sets remain minimal. Our theorem gives a affirmative answer to this product question within the entire Lawlor-Morgan regular-simplex family. It extends the isolated example \(\Y\times \Y\), the product of two 1-dimensional $\Y$ sets, proved in 2014 by the second author, simultaneously to all pairwise products \(S_m\times S_n\), and therefore produces a large new family of possible codimension-two singularities for Plateau's problem. The key idea of the proof is to find a new way to combine homology with paired calibrations in higher codimension. Instead of using only the currents associated with the facets, we consider all their nonzero $\FF$ combinations. The resulting complete family has enough algebraic symmetry to control uniformly the overlaps created by noninjective deformations.
item.dc:creator: Songsong Huang, Xiangyu Liang, Zaoyi Zhang

item.title: The Fourier restriction problem for biradial functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.27967v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the exact strong-type Fourier restriction range for the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$ on the class of $O(d-k)\times O(k)$-invariant functions, for every $d\geq4$ and $2\leq k\leq d-2$. This includes the critical estimates beyond the biradial Stein--Tomas endpoint left open by Mandel and Oliveira e Silva. The proof combines a weighted $L^2$ estimate for extension from a circular arc with the full two-dimensional restriction theorem. An appendix gives a direct proof of the classically conjectured range for axially symmetric functions on the whole sphere.
item.dc:creator: Shinya Kinoshita, Juyoung Lee, Diogo Oliveira e Silva, Shobu Shiraki

item.title: Remarks on space curve $L^2$ Fourier restriction
item.description: arXiv:2610.27968v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We re-examine and consider variants of the Fourier restriction theorem for space curves. In particular, we introduce a Stein--Tomas-type argument which recovers the sharp $L^2$ restriction theorem from classical oscillatory integral estimates, in the spirit of Arkhipov--Chubarikov--Karatsuba. In addition, we consider certain square function estimates which can be thought of as partial progress towards a space curve variant of the orthonormal Fourier restriction theorem of Frank--Sabin. These estimates are obtained by reducing the problem to a Kakeya-type maximal inequality, which we analyse using a formulation of the Bourgain--Guth broad/narrow method.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Claude Cuenin, Jacob Denson, Jonathan Hickman

item.title: One-Ring Bourgain Alternative And A 5-Decimal Bound On The Dimension Of Harmonic Measure
item.description: arXiv:2610.28037v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Improving theorems of Bourgain and Badger--Genschaw, we prove that the Hausdorff dimension of harmonic measure on any domain in $\mathbb{R}^3$, $\mathbb{R}^4$, and $\mathbb{R}^n$ for $n\geq3$ is at most $3-10^{-5}$, $4-10^{-7}$, and $n-(n-1)^{-(2n+6.12\sqrt{n})}$, respectively. The previous bounds in dimensions $3$ and $4$ were $3-10^{-15}$ and $4-10^{-26}$, while Bishop conjectures that the sharp bound is $n-(n-1)^{-1}$. The main difficulty in optimizing Bourgain's method is estimating non-additive $s$-dimensional Hausdorff-type contents when $s<n$ is close to $n$. Previous arguments used net contents associated to a fixed $m$-adic lattice, with $m$ large depending on $n$. We redevelop the dimension theory using pairwise disjoint cubes in general position and obtain a new estimate showing that one thin ring without large holes surrounding a cube makes it unlikely for Brownian motion to reach the cube before exiting the domain. A key feature of the construction is that the holes are round rather than rectangular. We also propose ten challenges on the dimension of harmonic measure that may provide accessible targets en route to Bishop's conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Michael Albert, Matthew Badger, Alyssa Genschaw

item.title: Spherical harmonics and infinitesimal projective transformations
item.description: arXiv:2610.28320v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Consider the space of $C^\infty$-functions on the two-dimensional sphere $S^2$ and its decomposition $\oplus\mathcal H_m$ into a direct sum of minimal rotation-invariant spaces. We consider elements of $\oplus\mathcal H_m$ as functions of two variables, a nonnegative integer variable $m$ and a complex variable $u$ (a restriction of such function to a set $m=k$ is a polynomial in $u$ of degree $\le 2k$). The group $\mathrm{GL}\,(3,{\mathbb R})$ of all matrices of order 3 acts on $S^2$, so its Lie algebra acts in $C^\infty(S^2)$ by differentiations along vector fields. We construct operators in $\mathcal W^\infty$ corresponding such differentiations and obtain a collection of differential-difference operators in $\mathcal W^\infty$. The expressions include shifts $m\mapsto m\pm 2$ and derivatives of order 4 in $u$.
item.dc:creator: Yury A. Neretin

item.title: Counting Bessel zeros and applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.28477v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish o-minimal definability results and develop point-counting machinery applicable to the zeros of a Bessel function of fixed non-negative real parameter. We also give an Ax-Schanuel theorem for Bessel functions of fixed (complex) parameters and exponential functions. We combine these to prove a sparsity result (weak Manin-Mumford) for points on an algebraic variety whose coordinates are zeros of a Bessel function of fixed (non-negative real) parameter. We apply this result to improve density results on spectral sets for the unit ball motivated by Fuglede's conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Gal Binyamini, Avner Kiro, Gady Kozma, Jonathan Pila

item.title: New Newton-type inequality and a unified perspective on Maclaurin's inequality via the inclusion relations of cones
item.description: arXiv:2610.28544v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The classical Newton-Maclaurin's inequalities for the elementary symmetric means are well known. In this paper, we derive a new class of Newton-type inequalities and generalize Maclaurin's inequality by connecting the elementary symmetric functions with their counterparts. Our idea is mainly motivated by the inclusion relations of G$\mathring{\text{a}}$rding's cones and $k$-convex cones.
item.dc:creator: Ning Cao, Xuanxuan Hu, Feida Jiang

item.title: On spatially irregular ordinary differential equations and a pathwise volatility modelling framework
item.description: arXiv:1902.01673v4 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This thesis develops a new framework for modelling price processes in finance, such as an equity price or foreign exchange rate. This can be related to the conventional Ito calculus-based framework through the time integral of a price's squared volatility, or `cumulative variance'. In the new framework, corresponding processes are strictly increasing, solve random ordinary differential equations (ODEs), and are composed with geometric Brownian motion. The new framework has no dependence on stochastic calculus, so processes can be studied on a pathwise basis using probability-free ODE techniques and functional analysis. The ODEs considered depend on continuous driving functions which are `spatially irregular', meaning they need not have any spatial regularity properties such as Holder continuity. They are however strictly increasing in time, thus temporally asymmetric. When sensible initial values are chosen, initial value problem (IVP) solutions are also strictly increasing, and the solution set of such IVPs is shown to contain all differentiable bijections on the non-negative reals. This enables the modelling of any non-negative volatility path which is not zero over intervals, via the time derivative of solutions. Despite this generality, new well-posedness results establish the uniqueness of solutions going forwards in time. Motivation to explore this framework comes from its connection with a time-changed Heston volatility model. The framework shows how Heston price processes can converge to a generalisation of the NIG Levy process, and reveals a deeper relationship between integrated CIR processes and the IG process. Within this framework, a `Riemann-Liouville-Heston' martingale model is defined which generalises these relationships to fractional counterparts. This model's implied volatilities are simulated, and exhibit features characteristic of leading volatility models.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: 2021 Mathematics PhD Theses, Imperial College London
item.dc:creator: Ryan McCrickerd

item.title: Invariant pseudo-unitary matrix ensembles and local statistics and conductance fluctuations of the DMPK ensemble
item.description: arXiv:2610.27532v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the DMPK ensemble, which models quantum transport in a disordered wire, and describe its limiting local statistics as the number of particles tends to infinity. In the metallic regime, as well as at crossover I, we obtain sine statistics in the bulk, Bessel statistics at the hard edge and Airy statistics at the soft edge. In the insulating regime, we prove localization around certain explicit deterministic positions with Gaussian fluctuations. This confirms and quantifies the predicted universal and localized behavior in the physics literature. At crossover II, we obtain explicit limiting kernels in the bulk and at both edges, which interpolate between these regimes. The hard edge kernel involves Legendre functions and, to the best of our knowledge, is new, while the bulk and soft edge kernels agree with those derived for the squared singular values of critically scaled products of independent Ginibre matrices. To explain these similarities, we construct a class of invariant pseudo-unitary matrices that is closed under taking products and use it to interpret the DMPK ensemble as the joint density of the spectral variables of a product of such random matrices. More generally, the latter takes the form of a polynomial ensemble of derivative type involving a second order differential operator compatible with the Legendre functions. Finally, we obtain uniform asymptotic expansions of the mean and variance of the conductance and prove that the DMPK ensemble admits universal conductance fluctuations, i.e. the variance of the conductance tends to $1/15$ throughout the whole metallic regime. This again confirms the predictions in the physics literature.
item.dc:creator: Dong Wang, Thomas Wolfs

item.title: Sharp Bounds for Nodal Sets of Steklov Eigenfunctions on Smooth Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.28391v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a sharp linear upper bound for the interior nodal length of Steklov eigenfunctions on smooth compact Riemannian surfaces with boundary, establishing the upper bound predicted by the Steklov analogue of Yau's conjecture in dimension two. On each fixed surface, we also show that the nodal length divided by the logarithm of the eigenvalue tends to infinity, uniformly over the eigenfunctions. We construct examples to show this divergence can be arbitrarily slow. These examples rule out every general lower bound by a positive power of the eigenvalue, in contrast with the linear lower bound on analytic surfaces by Polterovich-Sher-Toth. Moreover, boundary zero counts and both interior and boundary nodal domain counts satisfy sharp linear bounds for large eigenvalues. We also prove density estimates for boundary zeros on at least one boundary component and construct a fixed analytic cylinder on which another component remains free of boundary zeros along an unbounded sequence of eigenvalues.
item.dc:creator: Guiyu Xie, Cheng Zhang

item.title: Generalized mKdV Equation and Genus Two Jacobi Type Hyperelliptic Differential Equation
item.description: arXiv:2511.02621v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We generalized the mKdV equation in order that the static equations include ${\rm sn}$ differential equation. As a result, a good correspondence was obtained between the KdV equation and the mKdV equation.For general genus two hyperelliptic curves, we obtained differential equations for Weierstrass type and Jacobi type hyperelliptic functions. Considering the special case of $\lambda_6=0, \lambda_0=0$, Weierstrass type and Jacobi type hyperelliptic functions are different solutions to the same hyperelliptic differential equations. Then these solutions are connected by the special ${\rm Sp(4, {\bf R})}$ Lie group transformation.
item.dc:creator: Masahito Hayashi, Kazuyasu Shigemoto, Takuya Tsukioka

item.title: A Riemann-Hilbert approach to the computation of transform pairs
item.description: arXiv:2606.25252v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a unified methodology that integrates spectral theory, Riemann-Hilbert problems, and inverse scattering theory for the construction and numerical evaluation of transform pairs associated with linear variable-coefficient partial differential equations. The approach combines analytical formulae with numerical methods for ordinary differential equations and Riemann-Hilbert problems, yielding a hybrid analytical-numerical strategy for working with these transforms. Results are presented for transforms arising in the Dirac equation, demonstrating accurate computations, even in the presence of discontinuous coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Kaitlynn Lilly (Department of Applied Mathematics, University of Washington), Thomas Trogdon (Department of Applied Mathematics, University of Washington)

item.title: Lifting curved Kakeya sets to linear Kakeya sets
item.description: arXiv:2609.06299v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that many curved Kakeya problems, originally motivated by H\"ormander's oscillatory integral problem, lift to the classical Kakeya problem in higher dimensions. As a consequence, if the classical Kakeya set conjecture were true in all dimensions, the families of curves whose curved Kakeya sets have full dimension are dense among H\"ormander-type families. This is in contrast to the nowhere dense Bourgain's condition, which is a necessary condition for best-case curved Kakeya maximal function estimates. Furthermore the linear Kakeya set conjecture would imply a fairly complete understanding of Kakeya sets of quadratic curves, as first studied systematically by Wisewell. These results give a better understanding of a question posed by Guo--Guth--Nadjimzadah--Shen--Zhang, and they more generally show that the classical Kakeya conjecture in high dimensions rests on a broad range of curved Kakeya problems in lower dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Arian Nadjimzadah

item.title: Jackson and Bernstein Inequalities with Explicit Weight Dependence for Band-Limited Wavelet Approximation in Weighted Besov Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2609.35520v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove direct and inverse estimates for band-limited biorthogonal wavelet systems in weighted Besov spaces with Muckenhoupt weights. On functions recovered from their wavelet expansion along the dyadic tree of the unit cube, the error of approximation by a prescribed number of terms decays at a rate set by the smoothness-to-dimension ratio, and this exponent cannot be increased. Under a multiresolution condition, Bernstein inequalities hold at a single scale and on every multiresolution subspace, and the linear approximation spaces are identified with weighted Lebesgue--Besov intersections. All constants are explicit; the weight enters only through displayed powers of the Muckenhoupt characteristic.
item.dc:creator: Hung-Lung Lin, Kai-Cheng Wang

item.title: Weak type $(1,1)$ bounds for rough oscillatory singular integrals
item.description: arXiv:2610.02789v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In their seminal work, F. Ricci and E. M. Stein [Proc. Nat. Acad. Sci. USA 83, 1--3 (1986)] introduced the oscillatory singular integral \[ T_Pf(x)=\mathrm{p.v.}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} e^{iP(x,y)}\frac{\Omega(x-y)}{|x-y|^n}f(y)\,dy, \] and S. Chanillo and M. Christ [Duke Math. J. 55, 141--155 (1987)] established its weak-type $(1,1)$ inequality for smooth $\Omega$. For the rough variant, however, the weak-type $(1,1)$ inequality remained a long-standing open question. In the present paper, we settle this problem: specifically, we prove that the rough oscillatory singular integral is of weak type $(1,1)$ with $\Omega\in L\log^+L(\mathbb{S}^{n-1})$. Moreover, we establish weak-type $(1,1)$ bounds for the rough maximal oscillatory operator associated with $T_P$, a result of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Yanping Chen, Zhengyang Ji

item.title: Restriction estimates using multilinear Kakeya
item.description: arXiv:2610.17752v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We use multilinear Kakeya estimates to establish restriction estimates in higher dimensions. For sufficiently large dimensions, our approach yields better exponents than those obtained by a direct application of polynomial partitioning.
item.dc:creator: Xiangyu Wang

item.title: Fractional Besov-Sobolev Spaces on Chord-arc Curves
item.description: arXiv:2601.01348v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\Gamma$ be a bounded rectifiable Jordan curve, with complementary domains $\Omega_i$ and $\Omega_e$. For $1<p<\infty$ and $0<s<1$, we study the spaces $\mathcal B_{p,p}^s(\Omega)$ of harmonic functions satisfying \[ \iint_\Omega |\nabla u(z)|^p \operatorname{dist}(z,\Gamma)^{(1-s)p-1}\,dA(z)<\infty, \qquad \Omega\in\{\Omega_i,\Omega_e\}. \] When $\Gamma$ is the unit circle, these two spaces coincide with a fractional Besov-Sobolev space $B^s_{p,p}(\Gamma)$. The equivalence of boundary seminorms and harmonic energies on the circle raises a geometric question: which rough curves preserve these estimates? For every radial-Lipschitz curve $\Gamma$, we prove \[ \operatorname{Tr}_\Gamma\mathcal B_{p,p}^s(\Omega_i) =B_{p,p}^s(\Gamma) =\operatorname{Tr}_\Gamma\mathcal B_{p,p}^s(\Omega_e) \] whenever either $1 < p \le 2$ and $2/p - 1 < s < 1$, or $2 < p < \infty$ and $0 < s < 1/2 + 1/p$. For arbitrary chord-arc curves, the same trace identities hold when $1/p\le s<1/2+1/(2p)$. Taking $s=1-1/p$ yields an almost-Dirichlet principle for the unweighted $p$-energy on radial-Lipschitz domains when $3/2<p<4$, and on chord-arc domains when $2\le p<3$. For every $p>4$, this principle fails on a suitable radial-Lipschitz domain, showing that the upper bound $4$ cannot be increased uniformly over this class.
item.dc:creator: Huaying Wei, Michel Zinsmeister

item.title: Canonical forms for boundary conditions of self-adjoint odd-order differential operators
item.description: arXiv:2602.21234v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: It is useful to have canonical forms of boundary conditions in the study of the eigenvalues of boundary value problems and associated numerical applications. In [J. Appl. Anal. Comput., 2024, 14(4), {1854--1868}], a canonical form is given for self-adjoint differential operators of even order, with eigenvalue parameter dependent boundary conditions. In this article, we derive canonical forms for the remaining case, namely: for self-adjoint $(2n+1)$-th order differential operators with eigenvalue parameter dependent boundary conditions.
item.dc:creator: Yorick Hardy, Bertin Zinsou

item.title: Jacobi polynomials on the simplex of Hermitian matrices and zonal spherical functions on partial flag manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2607.25760v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce the radial part of the Laplace-Beltrami operator on partial flag manifolds and study its eigenfunctions, the elementary zonal spherical functions. These eigenfunctions can be related to orthogonal polynomials on the simplex of Hermitian matrices invariant under simultaneous conjugation by unitary matrices with respect to the complex matrix-variate Dirichlet distribution. Using a matrix-variate version of Koornwinder's method for constructing orthogonal polynomials in multiple variables from orthogonal polynomials in one variable, we construct a family of pairwise orthogonal polynomials in terms of Hermitian Jacobi polynomials and conjecture that some of these are elementary zonal spherical functions. Furthermore, we recall the definition of multivariate Schur polynomials and show how they can be used to obtain information about elementary zonal spherical functions. In particular, we give some partial results in the direction that the radial part of the Laplace-Beltrami operator on partial flag manifolds is strongly triangular with respect to the multivariate Schur polynomials. The elementary zonal spherical functions can then be constructed by applying the Gram-Schmidt orthogonalisation process to the multivariate Schur functions.
item.dc:creator: Teije Kuijper

item.title: An alternating Mizuno formula, modified gamma functions, and double sine special values
item.description: arXiv:2608.17545v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For $n\ge1$ and $\operatorname{Re}(x_j)>0$, we prove an alternating analogue of Mizuno's product formula: \begin{equation*} \prod\nolimits_{m=0}^{\infty} \left(\prod_{j=1}^{n}(m+x_j)\right)^{(-1)^m} = \frac{(\sqrt{\pi/2})^n} {\prod_{j=1}^{n}\widetilde{\Gamma}(x_j)}, \end{equation*} where $\widetilde{\Gamma}$ is the modified gamma function associated with the alternating Hurwitz zeta function. The polynomial factors are regularized using factorwise logarithms, and the formula establishes compatibility between this regularization and polynomial factorization. Applications include Gaussian and cyclotomic (Kurokawa--Wakayama type) evaluations; the single-factor case recovers the alternating Lerch formula, and a normalized ratio yields Wallis' product. A second group of results concerns an alternating double sine-type function. At nonexceptional positive periods, its positive-integer special values admit finite tangent-product representations. These products define locally meromorphic continuations $F_m$ in the period parameter. For $m\ge2$ and nonzero algebraic parameters, the continued values belong to $\mathbb P^1(\overline{\mathbb Q})$ at rational parameters and are finite, nonzero, and transcendental at nonrational parameters. We determine their orders at rational parameters and distinguish parameter continuation from fixed-period specialization at exceptional parameters. Additional results include Barnes factorizations of multiple alternating gamma functions, a Glaisher--Kinkelin special value, finite-product Stirling-type asymptotics, a symmetric two-parameter form of the known odd-integer multiplication formula, and an odd-scaling distribution relation for the alternating double sine-type function.
item.dc:creator: Su Hu, Min-Soo Kim
